title_en: Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of International Treaties and International Practices in the Trial of Foreign-related Civil and Commercial Cases

articles.content_en:
Article 1: When a People's Court hears a foreign-related civil or commercial case governed by the Maritime Law of the People's Republic of China, the Negotiable Instruments Law of the People's Republic of China, the Civil Aviation Law of the People's Republic of China, or the Maritime Traffic Safety Law of the People's Republic of China, and the case involves the application of an international treaty, the court shall apply the treaty in accordance with Article 268 of the Maritime Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 95 of the Negotiable Instruments Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 184 of the Civil Aviation Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 121 of the Maritime Traffic Safety Law of the People's Republic of China, respectively.
When a People's Court hears other foreign-related civil or commercial cases beyond the scope of the aforementioned laws and the case involves the application of an international treaty, the court shall apply the international treaty by reference to the provisions of the aforementioned laws. Where the provisions of an international treaty differ from those of the laws of the People's Republic of China, the provisions of the international treaty shall prevail, except for clauses in respect of which the People's Republic of China has declared reservations.

Article 2: Where a foreign-related civil or commercial case involves the application of two or more international treaties, the People's Court shall determine the applicable international treaty in accordance with the applicable relationship clauses contained in the international treaties.

Article 3: If an international treaty provides that the parties may agree to exclude or partially exclude the application of the treaty, and the parties claim to exclude or partially exclude its application based on their agreement, the People's Court shall support the claim. If an international treaty restricts the parties' right to exclude or partially exclude the application of the treaty, and the parties claim to exclude or partially exclude its application based on their agreement, the People's Court shall not support the claim.

Article 4: Where the parties invoke in a contract an international treaty that has not yet taken effect for the People's Republic of China, the People's Court may determine the rights and obligations between the parties based on the content of the international treaty, unless doing so would violate the mandatory provisions of the laws or administrative regulations of the People's Republic of China, or harm the sovereignty, security, and public interests of the People's Republic of China.

Article 5: Where the parties to a foreign-related civil or commercial contract expressly choose to apply international usages, and the parties claim to determine the rights and obligations between the contract parties based on the international usages, the People's Court shall support the claim.

Article 6: Where the laws of the People's Republic of China and the international treaties concluded or acceded to by the People's Republic of China do not provide for a matter, the People's Court may apply international usages. Where a party claims to exclude the application of international usages solely on the ground that they were not expressly chosen, the People's Court shall not support the claim.

Article 7: Where the application of international treaties or international usages would harm the sovereignty, security, or public interests of the People's Republic of China, the People's Court shall not apply them.
Article 8: This Interpretation shall come into force on January 1, 2024.
Article 9: Where any judicial interpretation previously issued by the Supreme People's Court is inconsistent with this Interpretation, this Interpretation shall prevail.
